title.en: Pyraminx legal-move state and turn player

summary: Drive a tetrahedral twisty puzzle from versioned discrete piece permutations and orientations, including distinct main-layer and tip moves, without inferring state from mesh transforms.
objective: A viewer can apply, preview, undo and replay supported Pyraminx moves while piece identity, orientation, notation frame and legal reachability remain exact.
intent_signals: animate Pyraminx tip and layer turns
example_prompts: Build a Pyraminx player where U and u are distinct legal moves and camera orbit never changes their meaning.
negative_signals: claim every tetrahedral puzzle uses this model
not_for: A universal model for all tetrahedral or corner-turning puzzles.
Competition scrambling, solving optimality or physical turning performance.

entities.name: Tetrahedral piece set
entities.guidance: Use stable IDs for the authored core, tips and every main-layer piece; attach colored or patterned facelets to their owning shell.

entities.name: Move-table manifest
entities.guidance: Store each supported token as an exact bijection over piece slots plus a discrete orientation update, with its inverse and affected-shell list.

entities.name: Notation frame
entities.guidance: Show the WCA reference orientation and distinguish uppercase two-layer turns from lowercase vertex-only turns independently of camera orbit.

state_contract.model: Start from a versioned solved manifest that enumerates piece IDs, compatible slots, discrete orientations and exact move tables for U L R B u l r b and their primes. Only states produced by those tables are accepted in this recipe.
state_contract.frame: Use the WCA reference orientation for labels: bottom face horizontal and front face toward the holder. Turn direction belongs to that puzzle frame, not the current camera.
actions: Parse only the declared tokens and reject unsupported suffixes.
Preview one affected shell group about its authored vertex axis, then commit its exact table once.
Undo with the stored inverse token; reset cancels preview and queue before restoring the solved manifest.
state_contract.authority: The discrete manifest owns slot and orientation state. Blender and Three.js transforms are derived presentation and never become the legal-state source.
state_contract.initialization: Solved state plus legal supported move replay only; arbitrary facelet import requires a puzzle-specific validator outside this recipe.

invariants: Every move table is a bijection on compatible slots and leaves every unaffected piece unchanged.
Each 120-degree move applied three times restores exact piece positions and orientations; a move followed by its prime does the same.
Uppercase and lowercase tokens have different affected sets but share the declared vertex axis.
A sequence followed by reversed inverse tokens restores the entire state exactly, including tip orientations.
Orbiting or changing display style changes no notation, piece identity or puzzle state.
motion_guidance: In Blender, author separate shells with pivots on the declared vertex axes, narrow visible gaps and enough illustrated clearance for the chosen display turn.
In Three.js, attach only affected rendered pieces to a temporary pivot, interpolate 120 degrees, commit once and rebuild settled transforms from discrete state.
Pause freezes presentation; reduced motion may commit immediately while keeping token, affected pieces and result visible.

object_craft.structure: Author individually identifiable tip, edge and inner visible shells around a simple hidden core; use consistent mating rims and explicit vertex-axis pivots.
object_craft.material: Use satin body plastic with separate colored or patterned face surfaces; retain labels or patterns so state does not depend on hue alone.
object_craft.articulation: Shell transforms are reconstructed from piece slot and orientation after each committed table.

object_craft.structure: Use a removable axis rod, affected-layer outline and ghost endpoint outside the puzzle silhouette.
object_craft.material: One high-contrast diagnostic accent distinct from face coding.
object_craft.articulation: Guide follows preview angle and disappears after commit or cancel.

physical_contract.scope: Legal discrete moves with authored turn presentation; no friction, contact force, corner cutting or manufacturing tolerance simulation.
checks: Move bijection and inverse closure are exact.
Illustrated shells do not visibly interpenetrate over the declared display turn.

creative_affordances: Use translucent, patterned, engraved or sculpted face treatments while preserving semantic piece/face identification.
Change turn easing and staging without changing move tables or commit semantics.
known_limits: The authored manifest, not the source, defines the exact piece taxonomy and move-table representation; it must be reviewed as implementation data.
No puzzle, move table, animation or reachability validator was run.

claims.statement: WCA Regulations 12e orient Pyraminx with the bottom face horizontal and front face toward the holder, use uppercase U L R B for clockwise 120-degree turns of the corresponding two layers, lowercase u l r b for clockwise 120-degree vertex turns, and primes for the counter-clockwise forms.
claims.scope: WCA competition notation at version April 1, 2026; it does not define this recipe's internal piece IDs, orientation codes or move-table implementation.
